name: sccache (shared compilation cache)
baseline: cargo build with no shared cache: every machine or CI job recompiles every dependency
verdict_reason: sccache can skip recompiling crates it has seen before, but it publishes no Rust timing numbers, and its own docs exclude much of a Rust build from caching: crates that invoke the linker (bin, dylib, cdylib, proc-macro) and anything compiled incrementally. Expect gains on clean CI builds of dependencies, not on local incremental rebuilds.
tier_reason: No benchmark numbers from the project or from any source found.
claimed_speedup: No published numbers; the README says it avoids compilation when possible
workload: None published: rebuilding Rust crates with a shared cache
platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows; local disk or several cloud storage backends
install: cargo install sccache (or a prebuilt binary); set RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache
one_liner: Compiler-output cache that wraps rustc; helps clean CI builds of dependencies but cannot cache binaries, proc macros or incremental crates.
how_it_is_fast: sccache sits between Cargo and rustc as a compiler wrapper. When an invocation matches one it has seen, it returns the stored output instead of compiling; a shared backend lets CI jobs and developers reuse each other's dependency builds.
use_it_when: Ephemeral CI runners that rebuild the same dependencies on every job
Teams sharing a cache backend across machines
skip_it_when: Local incremental dev builds: incrementally compiled crates are not cached
Workspaces dominated by bin, cdylib or proc-macro crates
Slow network links to the cache backend
caveats: No published Rust numbers found from the project or third parties
Hit rates depend on identical flags, paths and toolchains
tradeoffs: Cached crates must be built without incremental compilation
Storage and network cost for shared backends

evidence.quote: It is used as a compiler wrapper and avoids compilation when possible
Crates that invoke the system linker cannot be cached. This includes `bin`, `dylib`, `cdylib`, and `proc-macro` crates.
Incrementally compiled crates cannot be cached.
